events.text: The story of the night you were born will not die down. Pilgrims stop at the gate to look at you; a fortune-teller walks three days to see your palm and leaves without asking for silver. The grown-ups who keep you argue late into the night about what to do with a child the sky has marked.
events.arc: The Night the Sky Marked You

choices.text: Let the whole province hear of it

effects.log: By spring the story is in every teahouse from here to the capital. Strangers come to look at you sleeping, and some of them do not smile.

choices.text: Keep the child out of sight and say nothing

effects.log: The doors stay shut, the story is laughed off as an old wives' tale, and in time even the neighbours forget what they saw. Almost all of them.

choices.text: Give the child into a mountain temple's keeping for a few years

effects.log: An old abbot takes you up the mountain wrapped in a grey blanket. Behind the temple walls, for a while, nobody who means harm can find you.

events.text: Since the night the stars went out, dogs will not bark near you and candles lean towards your cradle. A wandering Taoist stops at the gate, looks at you for a long time and says only, "Before heaven and earth." The grown-ups who keep you do not sleep well after that, and they have a choice to make.

events.text: Three riders of the {exam_sect} arrive at dawn, their horses lathered as if they had raced someone the whole way. The eldest kneels to look you in the eye. "We have heard about the night you were born," the elder says. "So has everyone else. Come with us, and you will be safe behind our walls, and taught by the best."

choices.text: Go with the envoys

effects.log: You leave within the week, with a bundle and a new pair of shoes. No examination: the omen was the examination.

choices.text: Say no. You will choose your own road

effects.log: The elder looks at you a long time, then bows to a child of fourteen as to an equal. "The gate will be open," the elder says, and rides away slowly, looking back twice.

events.text: Two envoys come on the same day: one from the {exam_sect}, one from a sect nobody can name, who leaves before supper when the first one stares at him. The envoy of the {exam_sect} sets a jade token on the table. "Others are coming," the envoy says quietly. "Not all of them will ask."

choices.text: Take the jade token and go

effects.log: You leave within the week, with a bundle and a new pair of shoes. No examination: the omen was the examination.

choices.text: Push the token back across the table

effects.log: The envoy sighs and pockets the token. "Then train hard," the envoy says at the door. "Faster than you think you need to."

events.text: You wake in the dark because the crickets have stopped. A shadow is crouching on the beam above your bed, very still, a short blade in its hand. Whoever sent it has heard about the night you were born.

choices.text: Fight back with everything you know

ok.log: You do not remember deciding to move. When it is over the assassin is running across the rooftops, clutching an arm, and you are standing in the dark with your heart hammering. You are still alive.

fail.deathCause: an assassin sent for a child the sky had marked
fail.log: The assassin is faster than anyone you have ever fought. You wake days later with bandages round your ribs and a lamp burning by the bed, alive because someone came running.

choices.text: Roll off the bed and run for the window

ok.log: You run as you have never run, through gaps no grown-up could fit, and the footsteps behind you give up at the river.

fail.log: A hand catches your collar, and the blade catches your arm. You tear free and keep running, and the shouting of the whole street finally drives the shadow off.

choices.text: Scream and wake the whole street

effects.log: You scream until every shutter on the street flies open. The assassin melts back into the night, but not before the blade has found your shoulder.

events.text: In the crowd of the spring market a pedlar with kind eyes offers you a sweet. The hand that holds it out is too steady, and the other hand is under the cloth of the stall. You have seen that stillness before, in tigers.

events.text: A stranger in a plain grey robe falls into step beside you on an empty road. "Do you know what you are carrying?" {npc} asks pleasantly. "A root like yours is wasted on someone like you. I have been looking for one for thirty years." The qi coming off {him} smells of old smoke and the demonic arts.

choices.text: Fight {npc}

ok.log: {npc} did not expect a fight like that from prey. Bleeding qi from a dozen cuts, {he} flees into the dark, and your root is still your own.

fail.log: {npc} breaks your guard, and a palm lands on your dantian, and something is pulled out of you by the roots, slowly, like a nail from old wood.

choices.text: Flee with every step of lightness you have

ok.log: You run for three days over roofs and rivers before you dare to sleep. {npc} does not follow. A thief wants easy prey.

fail.log: {npc} is waiting at the end of the road you chose, almost bored. "Running only tires the root," {he} says, and puts a palm on your dantian.

choices.text: Buy {him} off with 1200 taels

effects.log: {npc} weighs the silver in one hand and your life in the other, and takes the silver. "For now," {he} says.

choices.text: Offer {him} years of your life instead of the root

effects.log: {npc} drinks the years out of you through a palm on your chest. You feel old in a way you did not before. But the root is still yours.

events.text: The inn is too quiet. In the corner sits {npc}, an elder with dead eyes who has not touched {his} tea, watching you the way a pedlar watches a fine bolt of silk. When you stand to leave, {he} is already standing in the doorway. "Bones like yours," {he} says, "should not walk around alone."

events.text: A salt merchant from the south mentions, in passing, a demonic elder named {npc} whose qi has grown strange and bright in the last few years, "as if {he} had swallowed a young sun." Every meridian you have left goes cold. You know whose sun that is.

choices.text: Swear to take it back

effects.log: You write the name on a strip of paper and keep it against your skin. It is the first thing you think of every morning for years.

choices.text: Let it go. You will make a life with what is left

effects.log: You decide, one evening, that the root is gone and you are not. The anger goes out of you slowly, like a tide, and leaves you lighter than you thought possible.

events.text: An old physician in a hill town takes your wrist and frowns. "Your root was taken, not destroyed. A stolen root never takes fully. It lives in the thief like a guest, and it remembers the way home." There is a pulse art, the physician says, that calls it back, if you are close enough to {npc} and strong enough to survive the calling.

choices.text: Study the Returning Pulse with the physician

ok.log: A year of needles and breathing in the dark. At the end of it you can feel your root out there, faint as a star at dawn.

fail.log: The art will not come. The physician sends you away kindly. "Come back when you are ready to listen."

choices.text: Pay the physician 600 taels for the written art

effects.log: The physician writes it out in a small careful hand and will not take a tael more than was asked. "Do not die using it."

choices.text: Let it go. You will make a life with what is left

effects.log: You decide, one evening, that the root is gone and you are not. The anger goes out of you slowly, like a tide, and leaves you lighter than you thought possible.

events.text: The Returning Pulse leads you north to a ruined shrine above a dead village, where {npc} has made a lair. You can feel your root inside those walls, turning in its sleep, as if it knows you are near.

choices.text: Watch the lair for a season and learn its habits

ok.log: You learn when {npc} sleeps, eats and meditates. When the time comes, you will choose the hour.

fail.log: One night the shrine's guard dog finds you. You get away, but {npc} knows now that someone is watching.

choices.text: Go in at once

effects.log: You walk up the broken steps in daylight, and the doors of the shrine are already open. {npc} is expecting you.

choices.text: Let it go. You will make a life with what is left

effects.log: You decide, one evening, that the root is gone and you are not. The anger goes out of you slowly, like a tide, and leaves you lighter than you thought possible.

events.text: {npc} sits on the altar steps of the ruined shrine with your root burning in {his} dantian like a lamp behind paper. "You came all this way," {he} says. "Good. A root fights harder when its owner is near. It will be a pleasure to finish this."

choices.text: Fight {npc} and call your root home

ok.log: At the last exchange you strike with the Returning Pulse, and the root tears free of {npc} and comes to you across the air like a bird to a hand. {npc} falls to the steps, emptied, an old person and nothing more.

fail.deathCause: the duel for a stolen root
fail.log: Your own root fights you from inside {npc}. You crawl out of the shrine at dusk and live, barely. Next time.

choices.text: Not yet. Walk away and grow stronger

effects.log: You turn your back on the shrine. {npc} laughs. You let {him} laugh: you will come back.

events.text: News comes that the one who stole your root is dead, killed by someone else or by the years. That night you dream of a fresh grave on a hillside, and of something small and bright waiting under the earth, calling your name.

choices.text: Go to the grave and take back what is yours

effects.log: You kneel at the grave until dawn, holding the Returning Pulse. The root comes up through the earth into your hands, cold and sorrowful, and settles home.

choices.text: Let it go. You will make a life with what is left

events.text: Your master {npc} asks for a spar in the empty yard, as on a thousand mornings. Today, at the hundredth exchange, {his} guard opens and does not close in time, and your hand stops an inch from {his} throat. For a moment neither of you breathes. Then {npc} sits down on the ground and laughs until the tears come. "Finally," {he} says. "Finally."

choices.text: Kneel and thank {npc} for every year of it

effects.log: You kneel in the dust. {npc} pulls you up by both hands. "Never kneel to me again," {he} says. "Teach someone. That is how you thank me."

choices.text: Help {npc} up and ask for one more bout

effects.log: You fight until noon. {npc} does not win again, and has never looked so happy losing.

choices.text: Bow as one master to another

effects.log: You bow, and {npc} returns the bow exactly, as to an equal. The disciples watching from the wall will tell the story for the rest of their lives.

events.text: Your spies have found one: {npc}, a young prodigy of a mountain sect, born with a root the teahouses sing about, practising alone by a waterfall every dawn. Nobody guards {him}. Nobody imagines anyone would dare.

choices.text: Take the root by force

ok.log: It takes a long, quiet night. At the end of it {npc} is alive and empty, and something bright and unwilling is turning inside you.

fail.log: {npc} fights like a cornered animal and gets away into the hills, screaming your face to everyone on the road.

choices.text: Drug {his} tea and work through the night

ok.log: {npc} never wakes during it. In the morning {he} will wake ordinary, and will not understand why for a long time.

fail.log: {npc} tastes the drug and spits it out, and is gone through the window before you can stand.

choices.text: Look at {his} face, and leave

effects.log: You turn away at the last moment. You tell yourself it was the wrong night for it. It was not.
